job.title: Chief Executive Officer, Central Coast Local Health District
job.description:
The organisation
Central Coast Local Health District (CCLHD) provides hospital and community-based healthcare to a fast growing and increasingly diverse population, through Gosford and Wyong hospitals and a wide network of community services. Guided by its vision of trusted care and better health for everyone, CCLHD is committed to delivering the care that matters most and to giving its people the support they need to do their best work.

The district’s next phase will require continued operational focus, deeper partnerships across health and aged care, and new models that support more people to receive care in the community while protecting hospital capacity for those who need it most.
 

The opportunity
This is a significant opportunity to lead one of New South Wales major Local Health Districts and shape the next chapter of healthcare for the Central Coast. Reporting to the Board, and accountable to the Minister for Health and Secretary, NSW Health, the Chief Executive will provide strategic, operational and cultural leadership across the District, ensuring the delivery of safe, high-quality and sustainable services within agreed performance and financial settings.

Key priorities for the role include optimising hospital care and patient flow to free up beds, expanding and improving care in the community and at home, and strengthening partnerships with aged care providers, local organisations and other community stakeholders. Using population health data to target where CCLHD can have the greatest impact, and improving communication about how people access care, will also be central to the role.

You will lead a complex workforce through a period of renewal, strengthening the Executive Leadership Team, clarifying accountabilities and building leadership capability across the organisation. You will maintain rigorous clinical and corporate governance, respond decisively to quality, safety and operational risks, and provide the Board with clear evidence and timely information to support effective oversight and decision-making.

The Chief Executive will also be a visible and trusted presence across the Central Coast. You will listen to the community, clinicians and staff, build productive relationships across the NSW health system and champion a more equitable approach to care. Particular focus will be placed on improving outcomes for Aboriginal people and increasing Aboriginal representation across the workforce.
 

About you
You are an accomplished health-system leader with substantial executive experience in a significant and complex service environment. You bring a strong record of operational leadership and an understanding of the realities of running busy hospitals while balancing patient access, quality and safety, workforce pressures, financial discipline and public accountability. Knowledge of the NSW public health system will be highly regarded, although outstanding leaders from other jurisdictions will also be considered.

You are comfortable leading in a highly visible environment and can act decisively when performance, governance or service issues arise. You use data to understand problems and set priorities, while remaining pragmatic about what can be achieved within constrained resources. Above all, you are an authentic and community-minded leader who builds trust. You work constructively with Boards, government, clinicians, staff, unions and external partners, communicate with clarity and create the conditions for people to contribute and perform at their best.

A tertiary qualification in a relevant discipline, or equivalent relevant experience, is required. Established Chief Executives and high-calibre step-up candidates with appropriate acting or enterprise-level leadership experience are encouraged to apply.
Most importantly, you are passionate about improving outcomes for the Central Coast community, including closing the gap in health outcomes for Aboriginal people, and you are motivated by the opportunity to lead lasting, positive change for the region.

This is an opportunity to lead a high-performing Local Health District and make a lasting contribution to the health and wellbeing of the Central Coast community.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer, NSW Environment Protection Authority
job.description:
• Lead NSW’s independent environmental regulator and environmental steward
  • Build trusted relationships across government, industry and communities
  • Sydney preferred, with regular travel across metropolitan and regional NSW


Lead the continued delivery of effective environmental regulation in NSW, building on a strong legacy of stewardship, trusted relationships and practical outcomes.

The organisation
The NSW Environment Protection Authority (EPA) is the State’s independent environmental regulator and steward. It works with Aboriginal people, communities, industry, businesses and government to protect, restore and enhance the environment of NSW and safeguard human health.

The EPA regulates activity across a broad and complex legislative remit, monitors compliance, investigates environmental harm and takes enforcement action where required. It also provides policy and legislative advice to government, supports emergency and incident responses, and leads work across priorities including waste, the circular economy and climate change.

With a highly committed workforce and a strong culture of stewardship, the EPA is focused on delivering its established reform agenda and translating policy into practical outcomes. This includes maintaining public confidence in environmental regulation while responding to increasingly complex environmental, economic and social challenges.
 
The opportunity
Reporting to the Board, the Chief Executive Officer provides executive leadership and direction across the EPA’s operations, people and resources. The role is accountable for governance, culture, organisational performance and financial stewardship.
This is a significant leadership and delivery mandate. Working with the Board, you will build on the EPA’s strong strategic foundations and lead the delivery of its established priorities and reform agenda. You will ensure the organisation continues to provide effective, efficient and evidence-based regulation, overseeing compliance, audits, investigations, enforcement and prosecutions while maintaining strong policy and legislative capability.

Central to the role is maintaining the EPA’s regulatory independence while working constructively and transparently with the Minister, Board and government. You will provide authoritative policy and legislative advice, maintain clear accountability and ensure there are no surprises between the EPA and government. You will also engage productively with industry, Aboriginal people and communities to improve compliance, minimise environmental harm and deliver better outcomes.

You will lead a passionate, values-driven workforce and continue the development and maturation of the executive team. Building on the EPA’s strong culture of stewardship, you will combine respect and collaboration with pragmatism, delivery discipline and accountability. You will also sustain the EPA’s commitment to meaningful engagement with Aboriginal people and ensuring their perspectives and outcomes remain integral to its work.
 
About you
You are an accomplished and strategic executive with strong intellectual capability and deep knowledge of environmental issues, relevant industries and the factors that shape industry behaviour. You bring substantial experience spanning environmental regulation, policy, law, science or a related field, together with a sound understanding of the Australian government and regulatory context.
 
You understand the distinct but complementary responsibilities of an independent regulator: exercising regulatory authority with integrity while remaining accountable to the Minister and working constructively across government. You can provide authoritative policy and legislative advice, lead complex implementation and engage productively with industry without compromising regulatory independence.

A credible and trusted relationship builder, you bring strong operational, financial and governance judgement and can make balanced decisions in complex and politically sensitive circumstances. Your leadership style combines intellectual rigour with empathy, generosity and sound judgement. You listen well, address difficult issues directly and respectfully, and can harness the commitment of a highly values-driven organisation to deliver practical and measurable environmental outcomes.

Upwards Living is an NDIS and aged care provider delivering personalised, culturally aware support that helps people live with greater independence, dignity and connection.

The organisation supports people living with disability, early onset dementia, psychosocial challenges and others who need support to live the life they choose. Its approach is built on relationships, not just service delivery, with a strong focus on culturally matched support, person-centred care and participant-caregiver relationships shaped by culture, age, interests and personality.

With values of compassion, integrity, collaboration, excellence and empowerment, Upwards Living is committed to lifting industry standards while supporting participants and staff to achieve positive outcomes.
 
The Opportunity
Upwards Living is seeking a Senior Service Manager to lead the delivery of high-quality Supported Independent Living services.
 
Reporting to the Head of Operations, this role acts as a key operational link between frontline teams and senior leadership. You will support Service Coordinators, Senior Support Workers and Support Workers to deliver safe, consistent and person-centred services aligned to participant goals, NDIS requirements and organisational standards.
 
This is a practical, service-facing leadership role with responsibility across service delivery, participant and family engagement, workforce performance, compliance, risk, incident management, documentation and budget oversight.
 
You will play a key role in ensuring services are well coordinated, staff are supported, participant needs are met, and quality and compliance expectations are maintained across a dynamic SIL environment.
 
You will:
 
  • Lead and support Service Coordinators and frontline teams
  • Oversee SIL supports in line with participant goals and care plans
  • Build trusted relationships with participants, families and stakeholders
  • Strengthen service quality, documentation, incidents and complaints
  • Support staff supervision, performance, training and development
  • Manage services within funding, budget and quality expectations

About You
You are an experienced disability services leader with direct experience in Supported Independent Living, disability accommodation or comparable residential disability services.
 
This is not a generalist disability leadership role. Upwards Living is seeking someone who understands the practical realities of SIL service delivery, including participant support planning, workforce coordination, family communication, incident management, documentation, safeguarding, funding parameters and NDIS compliance.
 
You bring:
 
  • Direct experience in SIL, supported accommodation or residential disability services
  • Previous leadership experience as a Service Manager or similar
  • Strong understanding of the NDIS framework and Practice Standards
  • Confidence leading frontline teams in a dynamic service environment
  • Experience managing incidents, documentation, risk and compliance
  • Strong relationship skills with participants, families, staff and stakeholders
 
This role will suit someone who is organised, calm under pressure and comfortable working close to service delivery. You will be able to balance participant outcomes, staff support, compliance requirements and operational performance while keeping quality of care at the centre.
 
What’s on Offer
 
  • A hands-on leadership role across SIL services
  • The opportunity to support quality, growth and service improvement
  • A values-led organisation focused on participant and staff outcomes
  • Direct impact across frontline teams and service delivery
  • The opportunity to strengthen team capability and service consistency
  • Remuneration aligned to the scope of the role
